en: The Questions of Milinda, Chapter on Investigation: 3.
The Question on the Manifestation of the Ultimate Limit (Koṭipaññāyana)
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that ‘the prior limit is not discerned’—what is that prior limit?
“Great King, that which is the past time—that is the prior limit.”
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that ‘the prior limit is not discerned’—is it, venerable sir, that every prior limit is not discerned?
“Some, great king, is discerned; some is not discerned.
“Which, venerable sir, is discerned, and which is not discerned?”

“Great King, it cannot be known that ‘in the past, ignorance was entirely, in every way, and in all respects non-existent’; this former limit is not discerned. But that which, having not been, comes into being, and having been, passes away—this former limit is discerned.
“Venerable Nāgasena, as for that which, having not been, comes into being, and having been, passes away—does it not then go to destruction, cut off on both sides?
“If, Great King, it goes to destruction, cut off on both sides, can that which is cut off on both sides be made to grow?”
“But, Bhante, I am not asking whether it can be increased from its limit; I am asking whether it can be increased [beyond that].
The Elder made for him the simile of the tree: “The aggregates are the seeds of the entire mass of suffering.
“You are clever, venerable Nāgasena! he replied.
The third question on the manifestation of ten million.
